<reason>A wins by defending stronger redress as bounded and evidence-based rather than perpetual. It directly answers deadline, proof, and privacy challenges with time-limited review, explicit eligibility standards, and protected disclosure. B raises a legitimate finality concern but repeatedly asserts that these safeguards cannot work without adequately explaining why. Most importantly, B never persuasively justifies extinguishing a claim established after a survivor’s death. Its concession of individual extensions also weakens its contrast between meaningful access and administrable closure.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A distinguishes preserving an inherited claim from approving it, and dividing one award from multiplying liability. B responds by shifting to continuing administrative costs, but does not show why those costs outweigh a proven claim or escape A’s proposed limits.</best_rebuttal>
